text:
Elliot Price: hey all — docs PR for data residency is blocked on a few specifics. can someone drop the finalized error codes + exact wording we should publish? also need 1–2 console screenshots (region pinning settings + what a violation looks like) and recommended troubleshooting steps we can put in the FAQ.

Wei Chen: +1. i can write around it but don’t want to ship wrong codes / guidance. especially around “pinned_region vs allowed_regions” and what happens on capacity exhaustion.

Kira Thompson: for Dedicated/Private pages: what do we say about Private/VPC? (i think “customer-controlled region” but need exact statement)

Brian Murphy: yep, we finalized the error taxonomy in the API standards doc but here’s the set we’re using in the gateway middleware.

Brian Murphy: Final codes (machine-readable `error.code`) + HTTP mapping:
- `RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH` (403): request was sent to a region that isn’t allowed for the org/project/workspace policy.
- `RESIDENCY_POLICY_REQUIRED` (403): enforcement enabled but no valid residency policy is configured (usually admin needs to set pinned/allowed).
- `RESIDENCY_POLICY_INVALID` (400): policy payload/config invalid (e.g., pinned_region not in allowed_regions, unknown region string).
- `RESIDENCY_ENFORCEMENT_BLOCKED` (503): control plane/policy evaluator unavailable and org is configured fail-closed. (this is rare; will show remediation to retry + contact support)
- `RESIDENCY_CROSS_REGION_FALLBACK_DISABLED` (409): request would have fallen back cross-region due to capacity/availability, but policy prohibits fallback.

Brian Murphy: Copy guidance (short):
- for mismatch: “This organization is configured for data residency in <pinned/allowed>. Send requests to <region base URL> or update your residency settings.”
- for fallback disabled: “Cross-region fallback is disabled by your residency policy. Retry later or request an exception for temporary cross-region allowance.”

Naomi Feldman: confirming semantics for docs: default behavior when pinned is NO cross-region fallback. only possible if customer has an approved exception + we flip the override flag for that org/project (and we audit it).

Monica Patel: from SDK side: we’re surfacing these as typed exceptions in python/ts. for troubleshooting, please emphasize:
1) check you’re using the correct regional base URL (eu vs us)
2) if using SDK, check `region` / `base_url` config isn’t set to a different region than the org policy
3) do not rely on automatic retries to “hop regions” — retries stay in-region and if pinned, fallback is blocked

Wei Chen: do we have the actual base URLs we want to publish? (people keep mixing `api.redwood.ai` vs `eu.api...`)

Brian Murphy: current public endpoints:
- US: `https://api.redwood.ai`
- EU: `https://eu.api.redwood.ai`
(we’ll add APAC later; don’t mention yet)

Chloe Martin: console screenshots: UI is behind `residency_console_settings` flag in staging. i can grab screenshots today. which states do you need?

Elliot Price: ideally:
- settings page showing “Pinned region: EU (eu-west)” + “Allowed regions” (if we show it)
- an inline validation error (e.g., trying to add US when org is EU-only)
- violation summary panel if it’s in the design

Felix Schneider: we have a simple “Recent violations” table in the settings panel now (timestamp, requested_region, decision, request_id). i can screenshot that too. it’s not super pretty yet but ok for docs if we blur ids.

Kira Thompson: for Dedicated/Private: can we say the feature applies to Hosted + Dedicated and for Private it’s “enforced by customer network boundary”?

Naomi Feldman: wording i’d use:
- Hosted/Dedicated: Redwood enforces residency at request admission + for downstream writes (logs/audit/analytics) within the selected cloud region.
- Private/VPC/on-prem: residency is determined by where the customer deploys the data plane. Redwood control plane features still produce audit events, but the data stays within customer environment/region by design.

Wei Chen: troubleshooting bullets for FAQ (tell me if wrong):
- If you see `RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH`: verify your org/project is pinned to EU and you’re calling `https://eu.api.redwood.ai`.
- If you see `RESIDENCY_CROSS_REGION_FALLBACK_DISABLED`: your workload hit capacity in the pinned region; retry with backoff OR contact support to discuss capacity / temporary exception.
- If you see `RESIDENCY_POLICY_REQUIRED`: ask an org admin to set a residency policy in Console (Settings → Security & Compliance → Data residency).
- If you see `RESIDENCY_ENFORCEMENT_BLOCKED`: retry; if persistent, open a support ticket with request_id + x-redwood-trace-id.

Monica Patel: looks good. add note: if they’re using our SDK, update to >= the version that includes the typed error (we’ll give you exact versions once merged). and include “print the `error.details` block” since it includes `allowed_regions`, `pinned_region`, and `request_region`.

Brian Murphy: +1. the error payload includes:
- `error.code`
- `error.message`
- `error.details.pinned_region`
- `error.details.allowed_regions`
- `error.details.request_region`
- `error.details.remediation_url` (docs link)
You can mention those fields for debugging.

Elliot Price: perfect. please drop the final screenshots in the shared drive or link them here once you have them.

Chloe Martin: will do. eta ~2 hrs. will post links.

Felix Schneider: same, i’ll grab the “Recent violations” table screenshot from staging and blur org + ids.

Kira Thompson: any gotchas we should call out? (like multi-workspace precedence or project override)

Brian Murphy: precedence (docs-safe): Workspace overrides Project overrides Org. If multiple are set, most specific wins. also note: policy changes can take up to ~60s to propagate due to cache.

Wei Chen: propagation delay note is important — we’re seeing confusion in support threads.

Naomi Feldman: please add a line: “Changes may take up to 60 seconds to apply globally. During rollout, some requests may continue to succeed/deny based on cached policy; audit events reflect which policy version was evaluated.”

Elliot Price: awesome, thanks all. i’ll update the docs PR today with the codes + troubleshooting and wait on screenshots.

Chloe Martin: screenshots uploaded: https://drive.google.com/…/residency-console-settings-eu-pinned.png and https://drive.google.com/…/residency-console-validation-error.png

Felix Schneider: “Recent violations” screenshot: https://drive.google.com/…/residency-console-recent-violations.png

Elliot Price: got them. thanks! i’ll blur a couple IDs before publishing. merging copy tonight unless anyone objects.
